content: Pityriasis lichenoides et varioliformis acuta (PLEVA), also known as Mucha-Habermann's disease, is an immune-mediated dermatological condition. It represents the more severe form of pityriasis lichenoides chronica. The disease is characterized by the presence of skin rashes and small lesions, which can vary in appearance and severity. PLEVA is most commonly observed in males and typically manifests during childhood. However, it can occur across all age groups and ethnicities. The disease may enter remission, either temporarily or permanently, though the course of the condition can vary significantly between individuals. Historically, PLEVA has been frequently misdiagnosed as other conditions, such as chickenpox or rosacea, due to similarities in the appearance of skin lesions. Accurate diagnosis often requires a skin biopsy, which provides definitive histopathological evidence of the disease. The prognosis for PLEVA is generally favorable with appropriate treatment. While the condition is not contagious, there is currently no definitive cure. Management strategies focus on alleviating symptoms and addressing underlying immune dysregulation. Treatment options include ultraviolet (UV) therapy, topical corticosteroids, and antibiotics. In some cases, a combination of therapies targeting immune, bacterial, viral, or dermatological factors may be necessary to achieve optimal outcomes.
